Schwann’s Claims (1839)




    1. The cell is the unit of structure, physiology,
       and organization in living things.

    2. The cell retains a dual existence as a distinct
       entity and a building block in the construction
       of organisms.

    3. Cells form by free-cell formation, similar to the
       formation of crystals.



                                                           Image: Deutsches Textarchiv   6
title: Schwann's Claims (1839)

text:
Three Speculative Claims




    1. Features are the fundamental unit of neural
       networks. They correspond to directions.
       These features can be rigorously studied and
       understood.

    2. Features are connected by weights, forming
       circuits. These circuits can also be rigorously
       studied and understood.

    3. Universality: Analogous features and circuits
       form across models and tasks.


   “Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits” [Olah et al., 2020]

Dictionary Learning

   Setup: Unknown dictionary A = [A1 , . . . , Am ] ∈ Rn×m with m > n.
   We observe samples y = Ax , where x ∈ Rm is k-sparse. We know neither x nor A.
   Claim: A is recoverable up to permutation and sign, in polynomial time, if:
                                               √   
     • Sparsity: k ≤ c · min m2/5 , µ logn n
     • Incoherence: |⟨Ai , Aj ⟩| ≤ √µn for all i ̸= j
                                           2
                                                    
     • Sufficient data: p = Ω m
                              k2
                                 log m samples with varying support
     • Well-behaved coefficients: independent, symmetric, bounded away from zero




   New Algorithms for Learning Incoherent and Overcomplete Dictionaries [Arora et al., 2013]

Compressed Sensing

   Setup: Known dictionary A ∈ Rn×m . We observe y = Ax , where x is k-sparse. We
   want to recover x .
   Problem: m > n, so there are infinitely many solutions to Ax = y .
   Claim: If A satisfies the Restricted Isometry Property (RIP), then

                                          min ∥z∥1     s.t.   Az = y
                                           z

   recovers x exactly.
   ℓ1 minimization finds the sparse solution; ℓ2 minimization does not.

   In the Claude Opus 4.5 system card:

title: Misaligned Intervention

text:
General Patterns in Circuits

     • High-abstraction features in middle layers, simple token features in early/late
       layers
     • Attention moves most information in early layers
     • “Default” circuits that get overwritten (e.g. “unknown person” → specific person)
     • Multiple pathways/shortcuts to the answer
     • Computation on special token positions (e.g. full stops, <assistant:>)
     • Confidence-reducing features (cf. negative name movers in IOI)
     • Many “boring” features active but not part of the core computation




   On the Biology of a Large Language Model [Lindsey, Gurnee, et al., 2025]

      • Expensive for large models
      • Sparsity is a flawed proxy for interpretability
      • Dataset dependent
